title: LA RSO and JCO no-fault eviction relocation assistance
requirement: For a not-at-fault eviction of an RSO or JCO unit, the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving notice and pay relocation assistance within 15 days. Not-at-fault causes include owner/relative occupancy, demolition and government order to vacate.
coverage_conditions: Not-at-fault evictions of units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance or the Just Cause Ordinance. Mom and Pop properties (4 or fewer units) and single-family dwellings owned by a natural person may pay reduced relocation.

conditions.text: units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO)

applicability.per_tenancy: Mom and Pop properties (4 or fewer rental units) and single-family dwellings owned by a natural person may pay reduced relocation; reduced amount only for owner, eligible relative or resident manager occupancy.
coverage_quotes: All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO).

Mom and Pop properties may pay reduced relocation assistance payments to their tenants for a good faith eviction for occupancy by the owner or eligible relative, provided that requirements in Section 151.30 of the LAMC are met.

exemptions: Resident manager replaced by another resident manager; eviction required by hazardous conditions from a natural disaster not caused by landlord negligence; landlord may offset accumulated rent against relocation assistance, except where a government order to vacate requires it.
penalty: Failure to file the Landlord Declaration makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO; a tenant may raise non-payment as an affirmative defense and may complain to LAHD or seek a private right of action.
quoted_span: All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO).

title: Resident Protections Ordinance relocation for demolition of Protected Units
requirement: A landlord terminating a tenancy to demolish a Protected Unit for new construction must file a Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD and pay relocation assistance at the higher of State (HCA) or City (RSO/JCO/RPO) amounts.
coverage_conditions: Protected Units demolished for the purpose of new construction within 5 years after the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict is filed; lower income tenants receive enhanced relocation.

conditions.text: Protected Units demolished for the purpose of new construction

coverage_quotes: The RPO only applies to Protected Units that will be demolished for the purpose of new construction.

penalty: Failure to comply with the RPO may result in financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
quoted_span: Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for the purpose of new construction within 5 years after the filing of the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD are required to comply with relocation requirements under the RPO. Failure to comply with the RPO may result in financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
interaction: Relocation must satisfy the State Housing Crisis Act (California Government Code § 66300 et seq.) or City law, whichever is higher.
